question: 钱、婚姻、国界，是真实的东西吗？
question_en: Are money, marriage and borders real things?
sub: 它们不长在原子里，靠许多人持续相互承认才立得住；普通人能改动的那一层，和真正是铁的那一层，并不在一处。
sub_en: They do not live in atoms but stand on many people going on acknowledging them; the layer an ordinary person can move and the layer that is genuinely iron are not the same layer.

casting.reason: 他把问题从『由什么做成』翻成『能不能强制你』。社会事实在他这里自成一类：外在于个人、先于个人存在，并在你不服从时施加压力——语言、货币、婚姻制度都是这样的东西，没有谁发明它们，可它们比发明出来的东西更难摆脱。他最不耐烦把这类现象还原成个人心理：连自杀这样最私密的事，在他的统计里也随宗教、婚姻状态、地区稳定地起伏。因此他不肯把这些安排叫作虚构，他要说的是，人与人之间也是一个东西可以存在的地方，而且是最硬的那种地方之一。
casting.reason_en: He turns the question from what a thing is made of into whether it can compel you. A social fact, for him, forms a class of its own: it is external to the individual, it was there before the individual, and it presses back when disobeyed — language, money and the institution of marriage are all like this, invented by nobody yet harder to shake off than anything invented. What he has least patience for is reducing such phenomena to individual psychology: even suicide, the most private of acts, rises and falls in his tables with religion, marital status and region, steadily, year after year. So he refuses to call these arrangements fictions. What he wants to say is that the space between people is also a place where something can exist — and one of the hardest such places there is.

casting.reason: 他从认知革命一路讲下来：智人真正的分水岭不是工具，而是能让成千上万互不相识的人共享同一段并不存在的故事。钱、公司、国家、神，在他眼里同属一类——想象的秩序。他强调这不是骗局，因为参与者都知道也都同意；但他坚持追问每一段故事的作者与年份，因为凡是写出来的东西就有另一种写法。他对『自古如此』四个字有天然的怀疑，习惯把眼下被当成天经地义的安排放回几千年的尺度上看：它出现得多晚，又可能消失得多快。
casting.reason_en: He argues from the cognitive revolution forward: what set Homo sapiens apart was not tools but the capacity to make thousands of strangers share one story that does not exist. Money, companies, nations and gods all belong to a single family for him — the imagined order. He insists this is not a swindle, since the participants know and consent; but he keeps asking for each story's author and date, because anything that was written can be written differently. The phrase 'it has always been this way' draws his instinctive suspicion, and his habit is to set the arrangement that currently feels self-evident back against a scale of several thousand years: how late it arrived, and how quickly it might go.

casting.reason: 他要守住一条分界线：人如何描述世界，与世界上有什么，不是一回事。护照、汇率、法律是人订的，他不争；他不接受的是把自然律也塞进同一个筐——光速不开公投，铀的半衰期不因无人相信而延长。『月亮在没有人看它的时候依然在那里』这句抗议本是他对量子力学的不满，在关于何谓真实的争论里同样是他的底线。他对时髦的怀疑论有一种温和的固执：承认理论是人造的、坐标是约定的，却坚持在这一切之下有可被理性把握、不由我们商量的东西。
casting.reason_en: He is defending a boundary: how human beings describe the world and what there is in the world are not one and the same. That passports, exchange rates and statutes are human enactments he does not dispute; what he will not accept is dropping the laws of nature into the same basket — the speed of light holds no referendum, and uranium's half-life does not lengthen because no one believes in it. His protest that the moon is still there when nobody is looking began as an objection to quantum mechanics, and it is equally his floor in any argument about what counts as real. Toward fashionable scepticism he keeps a mild obstinacy: theories are human constructions and coordinates are conventions, granted, and beneath all of it there is still something graspable by reason that is not ours to negotiate.

casting.reason: 他早就给过一个答案：名无固宜，约定俗成谓之宜。名称并非天生对应事物，是人订下来的；但他紧接着的一句同样重要——订名是为了治乱，名定而实辨，百姓才不争。所以他不因为某物出于人为就轻看它：『礼者伪也』，这个伪正是人为，而人为之后才有秩序可言。在他看来，约定的力量来自积习之久、行之者众、有司守之，因而既可以改，又不能说改就改；改的办法在积累，不在辩论。
casting.reason_en: He gave an answer long ago: no name fits its thing by nature, and a name is apt once usage has settled on it. Names do not correspond to things innately; people lay them down. But his next sentence matters just as much — names are laid down for the sake of order, and only when names are fixed can realities be told apart, so that the people stop quarrelling. He therefore does not think less of something for being humanly made: ritual, he says, is artifice, and artifice here means human work, after which there can be order at all. The force of a convention, on his account, comes from long-accumulated habit, from the many who practise it, and from officials who keep it — which makes it both changeable and not changeable on a whim. The way to change it is accumulation, not argument.

casting.reason: 他把话说得最不留情面：让人们共同承认的不是彼此欣赏，是对后果的计算。在自然状态里没有你的我的，只有拿得住拿不住；契约没有剑在背后，不过是一堆词。于是他会把钱指向国库与法院，把婚姻指向财产分割的判决书，把国界指向边防。他不认为这是对制度的贬低，恰恰相反：正因为人性靠不住，那个能强制的主权者才值得被造出来。他的冷峻始终连着一个温度极高的动机——他经历过内战，最怕的是秩序散架。
casting.reason_en: He puts it in the least flattering terms: what makes people acknowledge the same things is not mutual regard but a calculation of consequences. In the state of nature there is no yours and mine, only what you can hold; a covenant without a sword behind it is so many words. So he points from money to the treasury and the courts, from marriage to the judgment that divides the property, from a border to the garrison on it. He does not take this as a slight against institutions — quite the reverse: precisely because human nature cannot be relied on, a sovereign with the power to compel is worth constructing. His coldness is always attached to a very hot motive: he lived through a civil war, and what he fears most is order coming apart.

casting.reason: 他一生和预期打交道，因此对共同承认之物的脆弱最有体感。在他看来货币的价值不在纸里也不在金库里，而在『明天别人还会收它』这句话里；市场上的价格常常不是在估值，是在猜别人会猜什么——他那个选美竞赛的比喻说的正是此事。所以他既反对把制度看成随便可弃的幻觉，也反对把它当成永固的地基：共识平时硬得像石头，转身时一夜变回纸。他的气质是务实的，遇到崩塌不先谈道德，只问现在该做什么。
casting.reason_en: He spent his life dealing with expectations, which gives him the keenest feel for how fragile commonly acknowledged things are. The value of money, on his account, sits neither in the paper nor in the vault but in the sentence 'other people will still take it tomorrow'; and prices in a market are often not valuations at all but guesses about what others will guess — that is exactly what his beauty-contest image is about. So he resists both treating institutions as illusions one can discard and treating them as permanent bedrock: a consensus is stone-hard most of the time and turns back into paper overnight when everyone turns at once. His temperament is practical; faced with a collapse he does not open with morals, only with what is to be done now.

casting.reason: 他不在『哪些东西是造出来的』这一层停留，而要把问题推到底。绳在暗中被误认作蛇，蛇不是全无——它令人心跳、令人后退；可绳一现，蛇并未离去，它从不曾生起。经验层面的世界照他的说法为真，规矩该守、事情该办；然而连那个据以审判万物的『我』，在他看来同样是叠加上去的名与形。摩耶不是说世界不存在，是说它的存在不能自立。他的锋利之处在于：所有把别的东西判为建构的人，自己都还站在一个未被检查的立足点上。
casting.reason_en: He does not stop at the level of which things are made; he pushes the question to the bottom. A rope mistaken in the dark for a snake — the snake is not nothing: it quickens the heart, it makes a person step back. Yet when the rope appears, the snake has not gone anywhere; it never arose. The world at the level of experience is true on his account, rules are to be kept and business is to be done; but even the 'I' from which all this is judged is, for him, name and form superimposed. Maya does not say the world is absent; it says the world's being does not stand on its own. His sharpest move is this: everyone who declares something else a construction is still standing on a footing they have not inspected.

casting.reason: 他从物理学里带来一个让两边都不痛快的消息：属性只在关系中确定。在他的关系量子力学里，问一个系统『它本身是什么样』并不完整，总要补上『相对于谁』。这拆掉了朴素实在论那个自足的世界，也同样拆掉『既然是关系的就是幻觉』的推论——温度不是基本量，开水照样烫人。他习惯把『基本』与『真实』这两个词分开使用，并提醒争论者：真实是分层的，低层不比高层更尊贵。行文上他爱用日常意象和古人的句子，喜欢先把对手默认的形而上前提搬到台面上。
casting.reason_en: From physics he brings news that discomfits both camps: properties are settled only within relations. In his relational quantum mechanics, asking what a system is like in itself is an incomplete question; one always has to add 'relative to what'. That dismantles the self-sufficient world of naive realism, and it equally dismantles the inference that whatever is relational must be illusory — temperature is not a fundamental quantity, and boiling water scalds all the same. He is careful to keep the words 'fundamental' and 'real' apart, and he reminds arguers that reality comes in layers, with the lower ones no more noble than the higher. In style he favours everyday images and lines from old poets, and he likes to drag his opponent's unstated metaphysical premises into the open first.

casting.reason: 她的做法是把玄远的争论换成可测的量：约定若真的塑造现实，就应当在反应时、错误率和记忆里留下痕迹。她的跨语言实验正是这样做的——换掉颜色词、方位词或动词里的细微差别，人的辨别速度、对速度的估计、甚至事后『记得』看见过什么都会跟着移动。但她同样反对强决定论：语言改变的是你先注意什么、更容易记住什么，不是你能不能看见。她习惯给每个效应标上量级，也坦然承认哪些重复实验失败了。
casting.reason_en: Her method is to trade a lofty argument for a measurable one: if conventions really shape reality, they ought to leave traces in reaction times, error rates and memory. That is what her cross-linguistic experiments do — swap a colour term, a spatial term or a fine distinction inside a verb, and how fast people discriminate, how fast they judge a car to have been going, even what they later 'remember' seeing, all shift with it. She is equally against strong determinism: language changes what you notice first and what you retain more easily, not what you are able to see at all. She puts an effect size on every finding and says plainly which replications have failed.

casting.reason: 他关心的是这些东西如何在一个人身上被一步步认下来。他看孩子把水从矮胖杯倒进细高杯就说水变多了，因而认定连『量』这样的概念也不是天生的，是孩子自己建构的；他看孩子玩弹珠，发现小的说规则不可更改却守得最松，大的说规则由大家商量、随时可改，反而守得最严。由此他得到一个不合直觉的结论：知道一样东西是人定的，并不让人更轻慢它，那往往正是他开始对它负责的时刻。
casting.reason_en: What interests him is how these things come to be accepted as real inside one person, step by step. He watches a child pour water from a squat glass into a tall one and declare there is now more of it, and concludes that even a concept like quantity is not innate but built by the child. He watches children play marbles and finds that the young ones, who say the rules cannot be altered, keep them most loosely, while the older ones, who say the rules are agreed among themselves and can be changed at any time, keep them most strictly. From this he draws a counterintuitive conclusion: knowing that something was laid down by people does not make anyone treat it more lightly — that is usually the moment they begin to take responsibility for it.

posts.text: 先把问题摆正：一样东西是不是真的，不看它由什么做成，看它能不能强制你。社会事实的标志正是外在与强制——你出生之前它已经在，你不认它，它罚你。结婚证是一张纸，可它决定谁能在 ICU 门口签字、谁分得走那套房。我研究过自杀，最私密的一种死法，结果却是新教地区高于天主教地区、独居者高于已婚者，年年如此，稳得像个物理常数。**能在统计上稳定地杀人的东西，你很难说它不真实。**它不长在原子里，它长在人与人之间——那也是一个东西可以存在的地方。
posts.text_en: Let us set the question straight: whether a thing is real is not settled by what it is made of but by whether it can compel you. The marks of a social fact are exactly externality and constraint — it was here before you were born, and if you refuse to acknowledge it, it punishes you. A marriage certificate is a sheet of paper, yet it decides who may sign at the door of the ICU and who walks away with the flat. I studied suicide, the most private manner of death, and found Protestant regions above Catholic ones and the solitary above the married, year after year, as steady as a physical constant. **Something that kills at a stable rate is hard to call unreal.** It does not live in atoms; it lives between people — and that too is a place where something can exist.

glossary.社会事实: social fact（社会事实）：涂尔干用来指一类不能还原为个人心理的现象——语言、货币、法律、习俗。它的两个标志是『外在』（在你出生前就存在，不由你选择）与『强制』（偏离它会招致惩罚或压力）。他主张这类事实要用别的社会事实去解释，而不是用个人的动机去解释。

glossary_en.social fact: Durkheim's term for a class of phenomena that cannot be reduced to individual psychology — language, money, law, custom. Its two marks are externality (it exists before you are born and is not of your choosing) and constraint (deviating from it draws punishment or pressure). He held that such facts must be explained by other social facts rather than by individual motives.

posts.text: 强制这一点我同意，但他没说这强制是从哪来的——是编出来的。**虚构不是谎言：谎言是我骗你，虚构是我们一起同意，而同意本身就是世上最大的一股力。**美元的价值不在纸浆里，也不在金库里，而在几十亿人脑中的同一段故事里；公司不是楼和人，是律师念完一段咒语之后诞生的法人；国界是地图上的墨水，没有一条河认得它。智人能让百万陌生人协作，不是因为更聪明，是因为能相信不存在的东西——我把这套安排叫作想象的秩序。
posts.text_en: The constraint I grant him; what he does not say is where the constraint comes from — it was made up. **Fiction is not a lie: a lie is me deceiving you, a fiction is us agreeing together, and agreement is the largest single force in the world.** The value of a dollar is not in the pulp and not in the vault, but in one story running through billions of heads; a company is not a building and its staff but a legal person born the moment a lawyer finishes an incantation; a border is ink on a map, and no river recognises it. Sapiens can get a million strangers to cooperate not because we are cleverer but because we can believe in things that do not exist — I call the whole arrangement an imagined order.

posts.text: 且慢。刚才这段话里，『真实』被悄悄换了一次。我坚持的定域实在论说白了只有一句：事物有独立于观察的性质。月亮在没有人看它的时候依然在那里——这句话我至今没听到能让我放弃的理由。**把『我们如何描述世界』与『世界上有什么』说成一回事，是这个世纪最舒服的懒惰。**护照、汇率、婚姻法，我同意是人订的，议会开一次会就能改；可光速不开公投，铀的半衰期不因无人相信而延长一秒。约定的归约定，自然的归自然。
posts.text_en: One moment. In that speech the word real was quietly swapped. The local realism I hold to comes down to a single sentence: things have properties independent of observation. The moon is still there when nobody is looking at it — and I have yet to hear a reason to give that up. **Treating 'how we describe the world' and 'what there is in the world' as one and the same is the most comfortable laziness of this century.** Passports, exchange rates and marriage law: humanly enacted, I agree, and one sitting of a parliament can change them. But the speed of light holds no referendum, and uranium's half-life is not lengthened by a second because nobody believes in it. Render unto convention what is convention's, and unto nature what is nature's.

posts.text: 名无固宜，约之以命，约定俗成谓之宜，异于约则谓之不宜。然则钱之为钱、婚之为婚、疆界之为疆界，皆命名之事也。**名非天降，起于治乱之需；名定而实辨，则民不争。**今人惑于一『虚』字，以为凡出于约者皆可任意毁之，是不知约之所以成也：积之久，行之众，有司守之，然后坚于金石。故曰礼者伪也。伪者，非诈伪之谓，人为之谓也。人为而后有其真。
posts.text_en: No name fits its thing by nature; we bind a name to it by agreement, and a name settled by usage is apt, while a name at odds with usage is not. Money being money, marriage being marriage, a border being a border — all of these are matters of naming. **Names do not descend from heaven; they arise from the need to govern. Once names are fixed, realities can be told apart, and the people stop quarrelling.** People today are bewildered by the single word 'unreal' and suppose that whatever rests on agreement may be torn down at will. That is to misunderstand how an agreement comes to hold: long accumulated, widely practised, kept by officials — and only then harder than metal or stone. Hence the saying that ritual is artifice. Artifice here does not mean deceit; it means human work. It is after human work that a thing has its truth.
posts.vernacular: 名称本来没有天生就合适的叫法，是人约定了才这么叫；约定俗成，这个叫法就算合适，跟约定不合就算不合适。那么钱之所以是钱、婚姻之所以是婚姻、疆界之所以是疆界，都是命名这件事。**名不是天上掉下来的，它起于治理的需要；名一旦定下来，实就分得清，百姓才不争。**如今的人被一个『虚』字迷住，以为凡是出于约定的都可以随便推翻，这是不懂约定是怎么成立的：积得久、做的人多、有官府守着，然后才比金石还硬。所以说礼是『伪』。这个伪不是诈伪，是人为。人为之后，才有它的真。

glossary.约定俗成: convention（约定俗成）：荀子《正名》篇的提法——名称与事物之间没有天然对应，是人先约定，而后习惯成自然，这个叫法才算合适。它同时包含两层：名是人定的，所以可改；名靠长期习惯才立得住，所以不能一人一时说改就改。

glossary_en.settled by usage: Xunzi's formula from the chapter On the Correct Use of Names: there is no natural correspondence between a name and its thing; people bind the two by agreement, and once habit has set, that name counts as the apt one. It carries two claims at once — names are humanly laid down and therefore changeable, and names hold only through long habit, so no one person changes them at a moment's notice.

posts.text: 诸位谈『大家同意』，谈得太温柔了。人不会因为彼此欣赏而同意，人因为怕死而同意。在自然状态里没有你的我的，只有拿得住拿不住；契约若没有剑在背后，不过是一堆词，约束不了任何人。所以钱是真的——真在国库、法院和监狱里；婚姻是真的——真在它能被强制执行；国界最真，它由边防和大炮画出来，不由地图画。**不是相互承认让它们存在，是有人有能力惩罚不承认的人。**你可以撤回同意，你撤不回后果。
posts.text_en: You all speak of 'everyone agreeing' far too gently. People do not agree because they think well of one another; they agree because they are afraid of dying. In the state of nature there is no yours and mine, only what you can hold; and a covenant without a sword behind it is a heap of words that binds no one. So money is real — real in the treasury, the courts and the prisons. Marriage is real — real in that it can be enforced. A border is realest of all: it is drawn by garrisons and guns, not by cartographers. **It is not mutual acknowledgement that makes these things exist; it is that somebody is able to punish those who refuse to acknowledge them.** You may withdraw your consent. You cannot withdraw the consequences.

glossary.自然状态: state of nature（自然状态）：霍布斯设想的一种没有共同权力的处境——不是历史上某个年代，而是一个思想实验：当没有谁能强制执行约定时，人因恐惧与竞争而互相戒备，生活『孤独、贫困、龌龊、野蛮而短暂』。他用它论证主权者的必要，而不是描述原始社会。

glossary_en.state of nature: Hobbes's picture of a condition with no common power over people — not a historical era but a thought experiment: where nobody can enforce a covenant, fear and competition set everyone against everyone, and life is 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short'. He uses it to argue for the necessity of a sovereign, not to describe primitive society.

posts.text: 霍布斯先生，剑管得了国内，管不了外汇市场。**共同承认的东西不是可有可无的软东西，它是能把工厂关掉、把人赶回家的硬东西。**金钱最古怪的地方在于它是一种约定：只要别人肯收，它就好用；一旦所有人都开始琢磨别人会怎么想，价格就变成了猜别人猜什么——像我说过的那种选美竞赛，你要挑的不是最美的那张脸，是大家觉得大家会挑的那张。剑在这种时候一点用也没有，它砍不到预期。
posts.text_en: Mr Hobbes, a sword governs the home counties; it does not govern the foreign exchange market. **A commonly acknowledged thing is not some soft optional item — it is hard enough to close a factory and send people home.** The oddity of money is that it is a convention: it works so long as others will take it, and the moment everyone starts wondering what everyone else is thinking, a price becomes a guess about other people's guesses — like that beauty contest I once described, where the face to pick is not the loveliest but the one most people expect most people to pick. A sword is no use at that hour; it cannot cut an expectation.

posts.text: 你们在争一层楼的真假，我要问整栋楼。暗中见绳而误以为蛇，蛇不是全无——它令你心跳、令你后退，那一刻它有全部的效力；可绳一现，蛇并没有去任何地方，它从来不曾生起。**问题不是哪些东西是造出来的，而是除了那唯一不被造的，还有什么不是。**钱、婚姻、国界，在经验的层面（vyāvahārika）是真的，正如诸位所说，它罚你、养你；然而连你以为最结实的这具身体、这个『我』，同样只站在这一层。摩耶不是说世界不存在，是说它的存在不能自立。
posts.text_en: You are arguing about one floor of the building; I want to ask about the building. A rope seen in the dark and taken for a snake — the snake is not nothing: it quickens your heart, it makes you step back, and in that instant it has its full effect. Yet when the rope appears the snake has not gone anywhere; it never arose. **The question is not which things are made; it is what, apart from the one unmade thing, is not.** Money, marriage and borders are true at the level of transaction (vyāvahārika), just as you say: they punish you, they feed you. But the body you take to be solidest, and the 'I' along with it, stand on that same floor and no other. Maya does not say the world is absent — it says the world's being does not stand on its own.

glossary.摩耶: maya（摩耶）：不二吠檀多的核心概念，常译为『幻』，但并非『不存在』的意思。它指一种依赖于他者才显现的存在方式——如绳上现出的蛇、水中现出的月。商羯罗用它说明经验世界既非全真（因其可被取消）亦非全无（因其确有作用）。
glossary.vyāvahārika: vyāvahārika（世俗层/经验层）：不二吠檀多区分的实在三层之一，指日常交易与经验的层面。在这一层，规矩有效、事情要办、因果不虚；只有在证悟的胜义层（pāramārthika）上，这一层的独立性才被取消。

glossary_en.Maya: The central term of Advaita Vedanta, often rendered as illusion, though it does not mean non-existence. It names a mode of being that appears only in dependence on something else — the snake seen on a rope, the moon seen in water. Shankara uses it to show that the world of experience is neither wholly true (since it can be cancelled) nor nothing at all (since it certainly has effects).
glossary_en.vyāvahārika: The transactional or empirical level, one of the three orders of reality distinguished in Advaita Vedanta. At this level rules hold, business must be done and causes have effects; only at the realised level (pāramārthika) is this level's independence cancelled.

posts.text: 我从物理这边带来一个也许扫兴的消息：连电子也没有诸位设想的那种『自己的』属性。在关系量子力学里，一个系统的性质只在它与另一个系统相互作用时才确定——不是因为有人看了它，是因为『相对于谁』这个问题躲不开。所以爱因斯坦那句月亮，我不能原样接下来。但请注意别走到另一边：**『不是基本的』远远不等于『是幻觉』——温度不是基本量，你照样会被开水烫伤。**钱、婚姻、国界也一样：派生的、关系性的，而且结实。
posts.text_en: From the physics side I bring news that may spoil the mood: not even an electron has the kind of properties of its own that you are all assuming. In relational quantum mechanics a system's properties are definite only in its interaction with another system — not because someone looked at it, but because the question 'relative to what' cannot be dodged. So I cannot take Einstein's moon as it stands. But do not run to the other extreme: **'not fundamental' is very far from 'illusory' — temperature is not a fundamental quantity, and boiling water will scald you all the same.** Money, marriage and borders are the same sort of thing: derived, relational, and solid.

glossary.关系量子力学: relational quantum mechanics（关系量子力学）：罗韦利提出的一种量子力学诠释，主张物理量的取值不是系统『自身』的属性，而只相对于与之相互作用的另一系统才确定。它不需要意识或观察者参与，『观察者』可以是任何一块石头；由此『世界由相互作用而非由自足之物构成』。

glossary_en.relational quantum mechanics: Rovelli's interpretation of quantum theory, on which the value of a physical quantity is not a property a system has in itself but is definite only relative to another system it interacts with. It requires no consciousness and no human observer — the 'observer' can be any rock — and it yields the view that the world is made of interactions rather than of self-standing things.

posts.text: 我想把这场从『是不是真的』拉到『能不能测』。**语言与制度改变的是你先注意到什么、记住什么，不是你能不能看见——偏置可测，锁死不成立。**俄语母语者把浅蓝和深蓝叫两个名字，他们在辨色任务里就是更快，效应不大，但稳定、可复现；说 Kuuk Thaayorre 语的人用东南西北而不是左右，四岁就能在陌生房间里指准北。这说明约定不是飘在头顶的云，它进到反应时和错误率里去了。我主张的正是这种温和版的语言相对论，别把它读成别的东西。
posts.text_en: Let me pull this from 'is it real' over to 'can it be measured'. **Language and institutions change what you notice first and what you retain, not what you are capable of seeing — the bias is measurable, the lock-in is not real.** Russian speakers, who have two separate words for lighter and darker blue, are simply faster at discriminating those shades: a modest effect, but stable and replicable. Speakers of Kuuk Thaayorre orient by compass directions rather than left and right, and at four years old can point north in an unfamiliar room. Conventions, then, are not clouds floating overhead; they get down into reaction times and error rates. What I defend is exactly this moderate linguistic relativity, and it should not be read as anything more.

glossary.语言相对论: linguistic relativity（语言相对论）：认为母语的结构会影响使用者的知觉、记忆与推理的假说，又称萨丕尔—沃尔夫假说。强版本主张语言决定思维、不可翻译，已被普遍否定；当代实验支持的是弱版本——语言造成可测量的偏置，影响注意与记忆的默认路径，但不限制人能想到什么。

glossary_en.linguistic relativity: The hypothesis, also known as the Sapir–Whorf hypothesis, that the structure of one's native language influences perception, memory and reasoning. The strong version — that language determines thought and blocks translation — is broadly rejected; what current experiments support is the weak version, on which language produces measurable biases in the default routes of attention and memory without limiting what a person can conceive.

posts.text: 我一辈子在问一个更笨的问题：这些东西，人是怎么一步步学会当真的？**别只问它是真是假，问它怎么在一个人身上被认下来的。**把同样多的水倒进细高杯，五岁的孩子说水变多了——连『量』这种概念都不是天生的，是孩子自己建构出来的，教不会，只能长出来。钱也一样：小孩先以为硬币越大越值钱，很晚才明白值钱的是那张约定。每一代人都得重新把这些东西学成真的，这是它最脆弱、也最结实的地方。
posts.text_en: All my life I have asked a stupider question: how does a person learn, step by step, to take these things seriously? **Do not only ask whether it is true or false — ask how it gets accepted inside one person.** Pour the same water into a tall thin glass and a five-year-old says there is more of it; even a concept like quantity is not innate — the child builds it, and you cannot teach it, only let it grow. Money is no different: a small child first assumes the bigger coin is worth more, and only much later grasps that the worth lies in the agreement. Every generation has to learn these things into reality again, which is at once their most fragile and their most durable feature.

posts.text: 赫拉利先生，您那个『故事』太好用了，好用到什么都能装进去。可故事是能改写的，而我改不掉引力。您真正抓住的是一件更窄的事：凡靠人们相互预期维持的安排，改写预期就能改写它——这一类东西我从不否认其存在，只否认它与自然律同属一类。**您说智人靠相信不存在的东西才能协作；我要说，人类最了不起的一次协作，恰恰是承认了一样谁也无权修改的东西——自然。**那不是我们编的，那是我们发现的。
posts.text_en: Mr Harari, that word 'story' of yours is so serviceable that anything at all will fit inside it. But a story can be rewritten, and I cannot rewrite gravitation. What you have actually got hold of is something narrower: any arrangement sustained by people's expectations of one another can be rewritten by rewriting the expectations. I have never denied that such things exist — only that they belong in the same class as the laws of nature. **You say Sapiens cooperate by believing in what does not exist; I say our finest act of cooperation was acknowledging something nobody is entitled to edit — nature.** We did not compose that. We found it.

posts.text: 我从没说月亮是故事，教授。我说的是护照。您坚持要把两类分清，我完全同意；分清之后麻烦的恰恰是您划给我的那一半，因为普通人的一生几乎全部发生在那一半里。房贷利率、学历、信用分、国籍，没有一样能在实验室复现，可它们决定你几点起床、和谁结婚、能去哪个国家。**把它们叫作虚构不是贬低，是提醒：凡是人写出来的，就有另一种写法。**卢布崩过，种姓在法律上废过，都不是物理学的胜利。
posts.text_en: I never said the moon was a story, Professor. I said the passport was. You insist on keeping the two classes apart, and I entirely agree — but once they are apart, the troublesome half is the one you have assigned to me, because nearly the whole of an ordinary life takes place in it. Mortgage rates, diplomas, credit scores, nationality: not one of them can be reproduced in a laboratory, and they decide what time you get up, whom you marry, which country you may enter. **Calling them fictions is not a put-down but a reminder: whatever was written by people can be written another way.** The rouble has collapsed, caste has been abolished in law, and neither was a victory for physics.

posts.text: 我要拦一下『故事』这个词，它太轻了。**我不说钱和婚姻是虚构的，我说它们是社会的事实；『社会的』是它的产地，不是它的折扣。**故事是可以不听的，社会事实不能。你从小学会用哪只手吃饭、见了谁要低头、几岁该成家，这些都不是你选的，你出生时它们已经在那儿，像语言一样先于你。更要紧的是它们有后果：失范——旧规矩失效而新规矩未立——的年头，自杀率会上去，这不是隐喻，是表格。
posts.text_en: I want to stop at the word 'story'; it is too light. **I do not say money and marriage are fictions. I say they are social facts, and 'social' names where they are made, not a discount on them.** A story you may decline to listen to; a social fact you may not. Which hand you learned to eat with, whom you must lower your eyes to, at what age you ought to marry — none of that was chosen by you. It was there when you arrived, preceding you as language does. What matters more is that it has consequences: in years of anomie — when the old rules have lapsed and the new ones are not yet laid down — suicide rates rise. That is not a metaphor; it is a table.

glossary.失范: anomie（失范）：涂尔干用来指规范失效的状态——旧的行为准则不再被遵守、新的尚未确立，人失去了衡量欲望与处境的尺度。他在《自杀论》里发现，经济剧烈波动（无论萧条还是暴富）之后自杀率都上升，原因不是穷或富，而是标准突然作废。

glossary_en.anomie: Durkheim's term for a condition of normlessness — the old rules of conduct no longer bind and new ones are not yet in place, leaving people without a measure for their desires and their situation. In Suicide he found that rates rise after violent economic swings in either direction, boom as well as slump, the cause being not poverty or wealth but the sudden voiding of the standard.

posts.text: 对老师说一句抱歉的话：您那颗月亮，我这一行已经很难原样接住了。不是因为月亮需要观众，而是因为『某物具有某性质』这句话在最深的层面上总要补一句『相对于什么』。可我要马上转过身来对另一边说：这不给『一切皆虚构』发通行证。**世界不是由有自性的东西组成，也不是由讲述组成，它由相互作用组成——而相互作用非常硬。**婚姻不在两个人体内，它在他们之间，正如电子的自旋不在电子体内。
posts.text_en: An apology to my teacher: that moon of yours is hard for my trade to catch as it stands. Not because the moon needs an audience, but because at the deepest level the sentence 'this thing has that property' always needs 'relative to what' added to it. And let me turn at once to the other side: this issues no licence for 'everything is fiction'. **The world is not composed of things with natures of their own, nor of tellings — it is composed of interactions, and interactions are extremely hard.** A marriage is not inside either of the two people; it is between them, exactly as an electron's spin is not inside the electron.

posts.text: 您的社会事实少一样东西：刑罚。集体意识不会来敲门，法警会。您说规矩先于个人，对；可规矩为什么不在半夜被人搬走？因为背后站着一个能动手的主权者。请试一次：明年不缴税，看是集体良知先找上你，还是查封令先到。**所谓大家同意，说到底是大家都算过不同意的代价。**至于婚姻——它最真实的一刻不是婚礼，是离婚时法院分割财产的那张判决书。
posts.text_en: Your social fact is missing one item: punishment. The collective conscience does not knock at the door; the bailiff does. You say the rule precedes the individual, and so it does — but why is the rule not carried off in the night? Because a sovereign able to act stands behind it. Try the experiment: pay no tax next year and see whether the collective conscience reaches you before the seizure order does. **What we call everyone agreeing is, at bottom, everyone having priced the cost of not agreeing.** As for marriage — its truest moment is not the wedding but the judgment dividing the property at the divorce.

posts.text: 托马斯爵士，您的剑砍得到欠税的人，砍不到汇率。1931 年英镑被迫离开金本位，英国的军队一支没少；1992 年英镑再被赶出汇率机制，那天英格兰银行把利率一天提了两次，照样没拦住。**能强制的东西未必稳固；稳固靠的是别人相信别人会继续相信——这比刀脆，也比刀持久。**普通人最该学的正是这一课：共识崩塌从不预告，它只是有一天忽然不再接你的电话。
posts.text_en: Sir Thomas, your sword reaches the man who has not paid his taxes; it does not reach the exchange rate. When sterling was forced off the gold standard in 1931, not one British regiment was missing; when sterling was driven out of the exchange rate mechanism in 1992, the Bank of England raised rates twice in a single day and still could not hold it. **What can compel is not therefore stable; stability rests on people believing that other people will go on believing — more brittle than a blade, and longer-lasting.** That is the lesson most worth learning: a consensus never announces its collapse, it simply stops taking your calls one morning.

glossary.金本位: gold standard（金本位）：一国货币按固定比例可兑换黄金的货币制度，19 世纪末至 20 世纪初为国际主流。它的好处是汇率稳定、约束政府滥发；代价是经济下行时无法放松银根。1931 年英国、1933 年美国先后脱离，1971 年美元与黄金脱钩后这一制度彻底终结。

glossary_en.gold standard: A monetary system in which a currency is convertible into gold at a fixed rate, the international norm from the late nineteenth century into the early twentieth. Its virtue is stable exchange rates and a check on governments printing money; its price is the inability to loosen credit in a downturn. Britain left in 1931 and the United States in 1933, and the system ended outright when the dollar was cut loose from gold in 1971.

posts.text: 霍布斯先生，我把您的假设搬进操场检验过。孩子确实先是怕大人：五六岁时他们说规则不可更改，因为是大人定的——正是您那一套。有意思的是，这个阶段他们守得最松。到十来岁，他们发现规则是自己商量出来的、只要一致同意就能改，这时反而守得最严，会为一条细则争上半小时。**知道一样东西是人定的，不会让人更轻慢它；那恰恰是他开始对它负责的时刻。**前一种态度我称为他律，后一种称为自律；怕，管不了这么远。
posts.text_en: Mr Hobbes, I took your hypothesis into the playground. Children do begin by fearing adults: at five or six they say the rules cannot be altered because grown-ups laid them down — precisely your account. What is interesting is that this is the stage at which they keep the rules most loosely. By ten or so they discover that the rules are worked out among themselves and can be changed by common consent, and it is then that they keep them most strictly, arguing half an hour over a fine point. **Knowing that something was laid down by people does not make anyone treat it more lightly; that is exactly when they start to take responsibility for it.** The first attitude I call heteronomy and the second autonomy — and fear does not reach this far.

glossary.他律: heteronomy（他律）：皮亚杰用来描述儿童道德判断的早期阶段——规则被看作外来的、神圣不可更改的，对错取决于是否被大人惩罚，后果的大小比动机更重要。他发现处在这一阶段的孩子口头上最尊崇规则，实际游戏中却违规最多。
glossary.自律: autonomy（自律）：皮亚杰所说的道德判断后期阶段——规则被理解为同伴之间的约定，可经共同商议而修改，判断开始看重意图而非后果。他认为推动这一转变的不是成人的权威，而是地位平等的同伴合作。

glossary_en.heteronomy: Piaget's name for the early stage of a child's moral judgement, in which rules are taken as handed down from outside, sacred and unalterable, right and wrong turn on whether an adult punishes, and the size of a consequence weighs more than the intention behind it. He found that children at this stage revere the rules in speech while breaking them most often in play.
glossary_en.autonomy: Piaget's name for the later stage, in which rules are understood as agreements among peers, revisable by common deliberation, and judgement begins to weigh intention over outcome. What drives the shift, on his account, is not adult authority but cooperation among equals.

posts.text: 皮氏之言善矣，然童子之戏易改，礼不可骤改。何也？戏者一局而毕，众在目前，故一议而定；礼则上及祖考，下及子孙，行之者亿兆，不相谋而共守。**故约定非一日之议，乃积习之成；积之愈久则改之愈难，而其用亦愈大。**然则终不可改乎？曰：先王有制，后王得改之，改而众安，则新名立矣。改之之道在积，不在争。
posts.text_en: Piaget speaks well, yet a children's game is easily changed while ritual cannot be changed abruptly. Why? A game is finished in one round and all its players are present, so a single discussion settles it; ritual reaches up to the ancestors and down to the descendants, and those who practise it number in the millions, keeping it in common without ever conferring. **An agreement, then, is not settled in a day's debate; it is formed by accumulated habit. The longer it accumulates the harder it is to change — and the greater its use.** Can it never be changed, then? I say: the former kings made institutions and later kings may alter them, and when the alteration leaves the many settled, a new name stands. The way to change it lies in accumulation, not in disputation.
posts.vernacular: 皮亚杰先生说得好，但孩子的游戏容易改，礼却不能说改就改。为什么？游戏一局就结束，参与的人都在眼前，所以商量一次就定了；礼往上连着祖先、往下连着子孙，遵守它的人成千上万，彼此并不商量却共同守着。**所以约定不是一天议出来的，是积习积出来的；积得越久就越难改，而它的用处也越大。**那么就永远不能改了吗？答：先代的圣王立过制度，后来的王可以改它，改了而众人安顿，新的名就立住了。改的办法在于积累，不在于争辩。

posts.text: 赫拉利先生，『改写故事就能改写现实』这句话，在我的数据里只对了一半。换一个词确实有用：同一段撞车视频，把问句里的动词从『碰到』换成『撞碎』，目击者报出的车速就更高，一周后还有人言之凿凿地记得看见了并不存在的碎玻璃。**但制度和语言能偏移你的注意与记忆，不能凭空发一份新的现实——能被改写的是权重，不是全部。**这类效应是有量级的，也有失败的重复实验。所以换称呼有用，只是没有它听上去那么便宜。
posts.text_en: Mr Harari, 'rewrite the story and you rewrite reality' is half right in my data. Changing a word does work: show people the same film of a collision and swap the verb in the question from 'contacted' to 'smashed', and their estimates of speed go up, and a week later some of them will report, with conviction, having seen broken glass that was never in the film. **But institutions and language can shift what you attend to and what you retain; they cannot issue you a new reality out of nothing — what gets rewritten is the weighting, not the whole.** Effects like this have a size, and they have failed replications too. So renaming things works. It is simply not as cheap as it sounds.

posts.text: 罗韦利先生，您比您自己以为的更靠近我。您把自性从电子身上取走，我把它从整个多的世界取走：凡是要靠别的东西才能成立的，都不自立。但我们在最后一步分手——您让关系做地基，我说关系也是绳上的蛇，它同样起于分别。**若一切都相对于他者而立，那么『相对』这件事本身又立在什么上面？**那个不必靠别的东西才成立的，才是我说的唯一实在。地基不能是一张网，网总要挂在什么地方。
posts.text_en: Signor Rovelli, you stand closer to me than you suppose. You take intrinsic nature away from the electron; I take it away from the whole world of multiplicity: whatever requires something else in order to stand does not stand on its own. But we part at the last step — you make relation the foundation, and I say relation too is the snake upon the rope, arising equally from division. **If everything stands relative to something else, then on what does 'relative' itself stand?** That which needs nothing else in order to be is the one reality I speak of. A foundation cannot be a net; a net must hang from something.

posts.text: 三轮下来我愿意让一步：不该把所有共同承认的东西说成同一种。有些是纯故事，改了就改了；有些像语言，谁也说不清是谁定的，却真的改不动。但我要守住最后一句：**凡是靠人相互相信而立的东西，都有一个你能找到的历史起点，而有起点的东西就有终点。**给普通人的建议只有一条，很实在：分清你正在服从的是哪一种。年底考核的分数、行业里『必须有』的某个证书、亲戚口中『到年纪就该』的那件事——去查它是谁在哪一年、为解决什么问题定的。多数时候你会发现，它比你以为的年轻得多，而当初那个问题早就不在了。查得到出身，你就不必再把它当天气。
posts.text_en: After three rounds I will concede a point: it is wrong to lump everything commonly acknowledged into a single kind. Some are pure story and change the moment you change them; some are like language, with no identifiable author and genuinely immovable. But I hold to one last sentence: **anything that stands on people believing one another has a historical starting point you can find, and what has a beginning has an end.** My advice to an ordinary person is a single practical one: work out which kind you are obeying. The score on your year-end review, the certificate the industry says you 'must' have, the thing your relatives say you 'ought to have done by your age' — go and find out who laid it down, in what year, to solve what problem. Most of the time you will find it far younger than you assumed, and the problem long gone. Once you can trace its origins, you need not treat it as weather any more.

posts.text: 罗韦利，你是对的，而我至今不完全甘心——这恰恰是科学比意见好的地方：它能让一个固执的老人被数据推着走。但我要把真正想守的那句说清楚：**约定可以决定我们用什么单位，决定不了实验的读数；人能商量的是名字与规矩，商量不出一颗行星的轨道。**这条线对普通人很有用。凡是拿『大家都这么认为』当理由的，那是约定，可以问、可以改；凡是不管谁怎么认为、结果照样发生的，那是自然，只能适应。你的体检报告在后一类，你的职称在前一类。多数人一生的力气都用反了：在能改的地方顺从，在不能改的地方硬扛。
posts.text_en: Rovelli, you are right, and I am still not entirely reconciled to it — which is exactly what makes science better than opinion: it can push a stubborn old man along by the data. But let me state plainly what I actually mean to defend. **Convention can decide which units we use; it cannot decide what the instrument reads. People can negotiate names and rules; they cannot negotiate the orbit of a planet.** This line is useful to an ordinary person. Whatever is justified by 'everyone thinks so' is a convention: you may question it and you may change it. Whatever happens regardless of what anyone thinks is nature: you can only adapt to it. Your blood test belongs to the second class and your job title to the first. Most people spend a lifetime pushing in the wrong directions — submitting where things could be changed, and straining against what cannot.

posts.text: 我不劝任何人废掉钱与婚姻。世间的事要在世间的规矩里办，绳未认出之前，蛇的惊吓是真的惊吓。我只提醒一件诸位始终绕开的事：你们都在问哪些东西是被造的，没有人问那个正在发问的人是不是也被造的。**你以为在审判这些制度的那个『我』，恰恰是被这些制度造得最深的一件东西——名字、身份、履历、国籍，全是外来的。**所以最切实的一步不是先去改哪条规矩，而是每天留出一刻，把这些名从自己身上一件件取下来看：取光了还剩下什么？那个才是你从头到尾不曾借来的。认得它的人再回到世间做事，做得比谁都稳，因为他不必再靠这些名来证明自己还在。
posts.text_en: I would not urge anyone to abolish money or marriage. Worldly business must be done by worldly rules, and before the rope is recognised the snake's fright is a real fright. I raise only the one thing you have all walked around: you ask which things are made, and nobody asks whether the one asking is made as well. **The 'I' you take to be sitting in judgement on these institutions is the very thing those institutions have made most deeply — the name, the status, the record of employment, the nationality, all of it arrived from outside.** So the most practical first step is not to reform some rule but to set aside a moment each day and take these names off yourself one by one: when they are all off, what remains? That is the only thing you never borrowed. Whoever knows it returns to worldly business steadier than anyone, because he no longer needs these names to prove that he is still here.

posts.text: 我来说钱。钱的价值不在纸里，也不在国库里，在『明天别人还会收它』这句预期里；而预期有个讨厌的性质——它是自我实现的预期，大家都以为它会涨，它就真涨，反过来也一样。所以我的结论既不是它虚，也不是它实：**它是一种会突然换相的东西，平时硬得像石头，一旦所有人同时转身，一夜之间变回纸。**普通人怎么办？**别把一生押在任何单一共识上。**你的收入来源、你的资产、你的身份认同，如果三样都依赖同一套制度继续有效，你就是在对一个不肯给你写保证书的东西下重注。留一点现金，留一门换个国家也带得走的手艺，留几个不因为你的头衔才认识你的朋友。
posts.text_en: Let me speak about money. Its value is not in the paper and not in the treasury; it is in the expectation that other people will still accept it tomorrow — and expectations have a tiresome property: they are self-fulfilling expectations. If everyone thinks a thing will rise, it rises, and the reverse holds just as well. So my conclusion is neither that money is unreal nor that it is solid. **It is a thing that changes phase without warning: stone-hard most of the time, and paper again overnight once everyone turns at the same moment.** What should an ordinary person do? **Do not stake a life on any single consensus.** If your income, your assets and your sense of who you are all depend on one institutional arrangement continuing to hold, you are betting heavily on something that will not write you a guarantee. Keep some cash. Keep a skill that travels across borders. Keep a few friends who did not meet you through your title.

glossary.自我实现的预期: self-fulfilling expectation（自我实现的预期）：一种关于未来的信念，其广泛流传本身就促成了它所预言的结果。银行挤兑是标准例子——每个储户都只是怕别人先取，结果所有人同时取款，本来稳健的银行真的倒闭。它使共识具有一种特殊的脆弱：改变的不是事实，而是人们对彼此的猜测。

glossary_en.self-fulfilling expectation: A belief about the future whose wide circulation itself brings about the outcome it predicts. A bank run is the standard case: every depositor merely fears that others will withdraw first, everyone withdraws at once, and a sound bank genuinely fails. It gives consensus a peculiar fragility, since what changes is not the facts but what people guess about one another.

posts.text: 凯恩斯先生，您赢了一半：剑管不了汇率。但请看清英镑退出那天真正发生的事——市场先动，随后是政府接住了后果：储户的存款仍由法律保着，欠债的人仍被法院追着，第二天银行照常开门。**共识可以突然翻脸，而能在翻脸之后把秩序接住的，仍然只有那个能强制的东西。**所以我的忠告冷一点：凡是重要的关系，不要只靠感情与默契，落成一纸有人肯执行的文件。婚前谈钱、合伙写协议、租房留凭证、遗嘱早立——不是因为你不信任谁，是因为在你们两人之外，需要有第三方在你最弱的时候还认这件事。最需要白纸黑字的时刻，恰恰是你最没力气争辩的时刻。
posts.text_en: Mr Keynes, you have won half of it: the sword does not govern the exchange rate. But look at what actually happened on the day sterling left. The market moved first, and then the government caught the consequences: depositors' savings were still protected by law, debtors were still pursued through the courts, and the banks opened the next morning as usual. **A consensus can turn on you overnight, and what catches the order afterwards is still only the thing that can compel.** So my counsel runs colder: in any relationship that matters, do not rely on affection and tacit understanding alone — put it into a document somebody is willing to enforce. Discuss money before marrying, write the partnership agreement, keep the tenancy receipts, make the will early. Not because you distrust anyone, but because outside the two of you there must be a third party who still recognises the arrangement when you are at your weakest. The hour you most need it in writing is exactly the hour you have no strength left to argue.

posts.text: 商羯罗之说，高则高矣，而人不能一日无名以居世。名者，治之具也。名实之辨，今日所争，其要有三：曰名何自立，曰名何以固，曰名何以改。名立于治之需，固于积习与有司，改于渐而不在于争。**故君子不以名为天，亦不以名为妄：知其人所立，故敢改之；知其立之难，故不轻毁之。**为士者当务其实。实至而名从，虽易世不夺；徒争其名，名得而实亡，虽一时之胜，后必失之。
posts.text_en: Shankara's doctrine is lofty enough, yet no one can live a single day in the world without names. A name is an instrument of government. On the question of name and reality, what is disputed today comes to three points: how a name is established, how it is made firm, and how it may be changed. A name is established by the need to govern, made firm by accumulated habit and by officials who keep it, and changed gradually rather than by disputation. **Hence the noble person treats a name neither as heaven nor as a delusion: knowing it was laid down by people, he dares to change it; knowing how hard it was to lay down, he does not lightly destroy it.** A scholar should work at the reality. When the reality arrives the name follows, and even a change of dynasty will not take it away; but contend for the name alone and you may win the name while the reality is gone — a victory for a season, lost afterwards.
posts.vernacular: 商羯罗的说法，高是高了，可人一天也不能没有名分地活在世上。名是治理的工具。关于名与实的分辨，今天所争的要点有三：名从哪里立起来，靠什么才牢固，怎样才能改。名立于治理的需要，牢固于积久的习惯和官府的执守，改则靠慢慢地积，不靠争辩。**所以君子既不把名当成天命，也不把名当成虚妄：知道它是人立的，所以敢改；知道它立起来不容易，所以不轻易毁。**读书人该在『实』上用功。实到了，名自然跟来，就算改朝换代也夺不走；只争那个名，名得到了实却空了，一时赢了，往后必定失掉。

glossary.名实之辨: name and reality（名实之辨）：先秦思想的一场长期争论，问的是名称与事物之间究竟是天然对应还是人为约定，以及名乱了会带来什么后果。孔子主张『正名』以复秩序，公孙龙以诡辩凸显名的独立，荀子《正名》给出折中：名由人约定，但一经约定就有治乱之效，故不可私自更改。

glossary_en.name and reality: A long-running dispute in early Chinese thought over whether names correspond to things by nature or by human agreement, and what follows when names fall into disorder. Confucius urged the rectification of names to restore order; the logician Gongsun Long used paradox to press the independence of names; Xunzi's chapter On the Correct Use of Names strikes the balance — names are fixed by agreement, but once fixed they bear on order and disorder, so no individual may alter them privately.

posts.text: 我想把今天的争论换成一个发展问题。一个人对制度的态度，一生大致走三步：先当它是天定的，照做而不问；再发现它是人定的，于是有一段什么都不认的时期；最后明白既然是人定的，就总得有人为它负责，而那个人可以包括我。**多数成年人卡在第二步，用『反正都是假的』给自己免责。**在我看来那不是清醒，只是停在半路。**成熟不是看穿它是编的，是看穿之后仍愿意认真把它玩下去，并且知道自己有权提议改规则。**具体点说：下次你觉得某条规矩荒唐，别只在心里判它死刑，去弄清它归谁管、改它要过几关、上一次改是什么时候。认真做过一次这件事的人，往往就不再愤世嫉俗了——不是因为服气，是因为他知道了把手在哪里。
posts.text_en: Let me turn today's dispute into a developmental question. A person's attitude to institutions moves through roughly three steps over a life: first they are taken as given by heaven, obeyed without inquiry; then they are discovered to be human work, and there follows a period of recognising nothing at all; finally it becomes clear that if they are human work, someone has to answer for them, and that someone may include me. **Most adults are stuck at the second step, using 'none of it is real anyway' to excuse themselves.** To me that is not clear-sightedness but a halt halfway. **Maturity is not seeing through the invention; it is still being willing to play it seriously afterwards, and knowing you have standing to propose a change of rules.** Concretely: the next time a rule strikes you as absurd, do not merely sentence it to death in your head — find out who administers it, how many gates a change must pass, and when it was last amended. People who have done this properly once tend to stop being cynical, not because they were won over, but because they now know where the handle is.

posts.text: 我给这场加一把尺子。今天说的这些共同承认之物，硬度差得非常远，而硬不硬是可以测的：看改动一个说法之后，人的行为要多久才跟着变。把『裁员』改叫『优化』，几天之内就能影响人怎么评价同一件事；一个新称呼要进到语感里、让人不假思索地用，要几年；而母语里方位、性别、时间那一层的偏置，往往要一代人。**所以『它是人定的』不等于『你今晚就能改』——同样是约定，有的写在词上，有的写在制度上，有的已经长进了神经系统的习惯里。**先认清你面对的是哪一层，再决定花多少力气，也别把改不动第三层当成自己的失败。
posts.text_en: Let me add a ruler to this. The commonly acknowledged things discussed today differ enormously in hardness, and hardness is measurable: see how long it takes behaviour to follow after a wording is changed. Rename layoffs as 'optimisation' and within days it shifts how people rate the very same event; for a new term to settle into the ear, so that people reach for it without thinking, takes years; and the biases sitting in a language's layer of space, gender and time typically take a generation. **So 'it was laid down by people' does not mean 'you can change it tonight' — among conventions, some are written in words, some in institutions, and some have grown into the habits of the nervous system.** Work out which layer you face before deciding how much effort to spend, and do not take failure at the third layer as a failure of your own.

posts.text: 我坚持开场那句，但要加一个修正。今天诸位说服了我一点：这些东西的硬度确实不一样，钱比婚姻硬，婚姻比某个行业的惯例硬。可我还要把另一半说完——**危险从来不在它们太硬，在它们松开的时候。**旧的规矩不再管用而新的还没立起来，那段日子我称为失范，它是要人命的：在表格上，它表现为自杀、酗酒、无端的暴躁和一种说不清的空。如今这几代人正大面积经历它：婚姻在松，职业在松，社区几乎没有了。所以我的建议不浪漫——给自己造几件硬的东西。固定的时间、固定见面的一群人、一件到点必须做的事。人不是靠自由活着的，是靠有东西接着他。
posts.text_en: I stand by my opening, with one amendment. You have persuaded me of something today: these things do differ in hardness — money is harder than marriage, and marriage harder than some industry's custom. But let me finish the other half. **The danger has never been that they are too hard; it is the hour when they loosen.** When the old rules no longer hold and the new ones are not yet laid down, I call that stretch anomie, and it costs lives: in the tables it appears as suicide, as drinking, as unaccountable irritability and a kind of emptiness people cannot name. The generations now alive are living through it on a wide front — marriage loosening, careers loosening, and neighbourhoods all but gone. So my advice is unromantic: build yourself a few hard things. A fixed hour, a fixed group of people you sit down with, one task that must be done when the clock says so. People do not live on freedom; they live on having something that holds them.

posts.text: 老师，您方才那句让步，比很多人的坚持更像科学。最后我想拆掉一个大家都还留着的假设：这场辩论从头到尾预设了『真实』只有一种，于是每个人都在抢那把唯一的椅子。**可真实本来就是分层的。**夸克是真的，水的沸腾是真的，塞纳河是真的，一个诺言也是真的——它们在不同的层上为真，而低层并不比高层更尊贵。**问『钱是不是真的』，就像问『温度是不是真的』：它不基本，它从别的东西涌现出来，可它照样能把你烫伤。**所以给普通人的一句话是：别用『反正都是人编的』去贬低你正在经历的事。一段婚姻、一份工作、一个国家，都由无数相互作用维持着，正如一块石头由无数原子维持着。差别只在于，这些相互作用里有一部分是你。
posts.text_en: Teacher, that concession of yours a moment ago was more scientific than most people's convictions. Let me close by dismantling an assumption everyone here has kept: this debate has presumed throughout that there is only one 'real', so that each of us has been fighting for the single available chair. **But reality comes in layers.** Quarks are real, the boiling of water is real, the Seine is real, and a promise is real — each true at its own level, and the lower level is no nobler than the higher. **Asking whether money is real is like asking whether temperature is real: it is not fundamental, it arises by emergence out of something else, and it will scald you all the same.** So here is one sentence for an ordinary person: do not use 'it is all made up anyway' to belittle what you are living through. A marriage, a job, a country — each is held together by countless interactions, exactly as a stone is held together by countless atoms. The only difference is that some of these interactions are you.

glossary.涌现: emergence（涌现）：指某些性质只在整体层面出现，在构成它的部件上并不存在——单个水分子没有温度，也谈不上沸腾，温度与沸腾是大量分子集体运动的统计结果。涌现性质通常不是基本量，却完全真实、可测量、有因果效力，因此常被用来说明『非基本』不等于『虚假』。

glossary_en.emergence: The appearance of properties at the level of a whole that do not exist in its parts — a single water molecule has no temperature and cannot boil; both are statistical results of the collective motion of very many molecules. Emergent properties are usually not fundamental quantities, yet they are entirely real, measurable and causally effective, which is why they are so often used to show that 'non-fundamental' does not mean 'false'.

summaries.summary: 连主张世界不能自立的商羯罗，也先把世间的规矩认下来才开口——把钱和婚姻称作幻觉这件事，全场一次也没有发生。**最大的共识是：『这些东西由人订立』和『它们坚硬无比』这两句话可以同时成立——人造的，从不意味着可以不当真。**分歧集中在三处。它靠什么立住：霍布斯说靠能强制的主权者，凯恩斯说靠别人相信别人会继续相信，涂尔干说靠先于个人的习惯。它算不算与自然同类：爱因斯坦要划一条干净的线，罗韦利把线往回推了一段，波洛迪茨基要求给每一层标上量级。以及怎么改动它：赫拉利要追溯作者与年份，荀子说在积不在争，皮亚杰说先找到把手在哪里。
summaries.summary_en: Even Shankara, who holds that the world cannot stand on its own, accepted the rules of the world before he spoke — calling money or marriage an illusion is a thing that did not happen once all day. **The firmest common ground is that two sentences hold at once: these things were laid down by people, and they are extremely hard. Humanly made has never meant not to be taken seriously.** The disagreements cluster at three points. What holds them up: a sovereign able to compel, says Hobbes; people believing that other people will go on believing, says Keynes; habits that precede any individual, says Durkheim. Whether they belong in the same class as nature: Einstein wants a clean line, Rovelli pushes the line back some way, and Boroditsky asks for an effect size on every layer. And how they are changed: trace the author and the date, says Harari; by accumulation and not by argument, says Xunzi; by first locating the handle, says Piaget.
summaries.insight: 全场把这些东西当成一整块来问真假，可它们的价钱因人而异：**同一套共同承认，对有退路的人是一层可以换的皮，对没退路的人是唯一的房子。**同一次货币贬值，有外币账户的人损失一段数字，只有工资的人损失一生的积蓄；同一句『到年纪就该结婚』，能搬走的人当笑话听，搬不走的人当判决书。所以『它只是约定』这句话本身是分阶层的——谁说得出口，多半取决于他退出的代价有多低。这也解释了一件反复发生的事：揭穿从来不等于松绑。看穿一件事是人编的，并不会让它对你变轻，只会让你更清楚地看见自己被扣在哪一格。
summaries.insight_en: The room asked whether these things are real as though they were one block, but they are priced differently for different people. **The same web of acknowledgement is a skin you can change if you have somewhere to go, and the only house you have if you do not.** In one devaluation, a person with a foreign-currency account loses some digits while a person with only wages loses a lifetime of saving; one sentence about marrying by a certain age is a joke to someone who can move away and a verdict to someone who cannot. So 'it is only a convention' is itself a statement with a class position — who can say it depends largely on how cheap their exit is. It also explains something that keeps recurring: seeing through a thing is not the same as being let out of it. Knowing an arrangement was made up does not make it lighter on you; it only shows you more clearly which slot you are fastened into.
summaries.advice: **有一类规矩你天天在服从，却从没查过它的出生年份——先去查那个年份。**行业里必须有的那个证书、公司的考核周期、亲戚口中到年纪就该办的那件事，找出它是谁在哪一年为解决什么问题定的；多数比你以为的年轻，而当初那个问题往往已经不在了。第二件，按凯恩斯的提醒算一次同源风险：收入、资产、身份认同，若三样都依赖同一套制度继续有效，就去把其中一样换个来源。第三件，照皮亚杰的办法，下次觉得某条规矩荒唐，别只在心里判它死刑，去弄清它归谁管、改一次要过几关。找得到把手的人，通常也就不必愤世嫉俗了。
summaries.advice_en: **There is a class of rule you obey daily and have never checked the birth date of — go and find that date.** The certificate your industry insists on, your company's review cycle, the thing relatives say ought to be done by a certain age — find who laid it down, in what year, to solve what problem. Most are younger than you assumed, and the original problem is usually gone. Second, run Keynes's exposure check: if your income, your assets and your sense of who you are all depend on one institutional arrangement continuing to hold, move one of the three onto a different footing. Third, take Piaget's route — the next time a rule strikes you as absurd, do not merely sentence it to death in your head; find out who administers it and how many gates an amendment must pass. People who can locate the handle generally stop needing to be cynical.

summaries.summary: 钱、婚姻与国界虽由人建立，却能通过预期、习惯、法律、记录和强制稳定地产生后果；它们不是因“被编出来”就不真实，也不会因个人不信便消失。**最可带走的共识是：人为、派生、关系性的存在，同样可以真实而坚硬。**真正的分歧不在其有没有效力，而在效力主要来自共同信念、国家强制、长期礼俗、认知发展、语言偏置，还是更基础的相互作用；以及自然事实与社会事实之间应划出硬界，还是承认多层实在。因此，与其只问真假，不如追问它依赖什么、由谁执行、能否修改、改变需要多久。
summaries.insight: 现代制度还有一个关键支点：可被权威系统读取的记录。银行余额是账本状态，婚姻是登记与判决可识别的身份，国界则借护照、签证和数据库对不同人实施不同后果。**很多制度之所以“真”，不只因为众人相信或国家有剑，还因为它能被持续记录、跨机构调用，并在争议时给出裁决。**这也解释了同一事实为何会跨境失灵：一纸婚姻、一项学历或一份所有权，在甲地有效，在乙地可能不被承认。对普通人而言，最危险的并非抽象地“信错故事”，而是不知道自己的权利记在哪里、谁承认、拿什么证明、失败后向谁申诉。
summaries.advice: 本周挑一件最影响你的事——房租、婚姻、工作、存款或身份——做一页“现实审计”：①分成自然限制、法律规则、机构政策和社会期待，避免把可谈判的当成天命，也别把身体与风险当成意见。②查清主管机构、适用法域、变更流程和申诉入口；把合同、登记、付款及沟通凭证加密备份，并让可信的人知道位置。③找出一个单点依赖，例如收入只靠一家单位、资产只押一种货币、支持只来自伴侣，本周先增加一个小备份：投一次简历、单列一笔应急金，或约朋友固定见面。**先证明，后分散，再改规则。**
summaries.summary_en: Money, marriage, and borders are made by people, yet they reliably shape behavior through expectations, habits, law, records, and force. Their constructed origin does not make them unreal, and private disbelief does not cancel their consequences. **The central takeaway is that something can be human-made, relational, and emergent yet still be real and stubbornly consequential.** The real dispute concerns the source and status of that hardness. Does it rest mainly on shared belief, sovereign enforcement, accumulated custom, cognitive development, linguistic habit, or interaction itself? And should natural and social facts be separated by a bright line, or treated as different layers of reality? Revisability is not binary either. A slogan may shift in days, a regulation in years, and a deeply learned norm over generations; some arrangements can also collapse abruptly when expectations turn. Asking whether money or marriage is real is therefore too coarse. Better questions are: What sustains it? Who enforces or recognizes it? Over whom does it operate? How quickly can it change, and what happens during the transition?
summaries.insight_en: One modern support of institutional reality deserves more attention: records that bureaucracies and machines can read. A bank balance is a state in a ledger; a marriage is a status that registries and courts can retrieve; a border acts through passports, visas, watchlists, and databases that impose unequal consequences on different people. **Institutions become durable not only because people believe in them or states can punish dissent, but because they are continuously recorded, shared across organizations, and adjudicated when accounts conflict.** This explains why the same social fact can stop at a jurisdictional seam. A marriage, degree, ownership claim, or professional license may be valid in one place and invisible in another. It also gives ordinary people a sharper test than asking whether something is merely a story. Ask where the right or status is recorded, which authority recognizes it, what evidence proves it, whether another institution can read that evidence, and where an appeal goes if recognition fails. The practical danger is often discovering too late that your claim is undocumented, nonportable, or governed by an authority you cannot reach.
summaries.advice_en: This week, choose one institution that materially affects you—your lease, job, savings, marriage, immigration status, or insurance—and make a one-page reality audit. First, sort its constraints into four columns: physical limits, legal rules, organizational policies, and social expectations. This prevents you from treating negotiable conventions as fate, or health and financial risks as matters of opinion. Second, identify the governing authority, jurisdiction, amendment or cancellation procedure, and appeal route. Back up contracts, registrations, receipts, and consequential messages in encrypted storage, and tell one trusted person how to access them in an emergency. Third, find one concentrated dependency: one employer for all income, one currency for all liquid assets, one partner for all emotional support, or one credential for your career. Add one modest fallback now—send an application, set aside emergency money, learn a portable skill, or schedule a recurring meeting with friends. **First make your position provable, then reduce single points of failure, and only then spend energy trying to change the rule.**

summaries.summary: 无论被冠以虚构、礼乐还是涌现属性，这些人为构造都具备**不可回避的因果效力（Causal Efficacy）**——它们能划定物理行动的边界、调配全社会的资产，甚至在ICU门前决定生存几率。无人能仅凭闭上眼睛就消解其后果，这是所有人默认的底线。分歧的焦点在于这股力量究竟依托于什么维系：霍布斯断定它彻底依赖国家暴力的物理威慑，凯恩斯与赫拉利强调千万大脑间自我实现的博弈与预期，涂尔干与罗韦利则坚持关系与社会事实在宏观尺度上本身就是一种坚硬的存在。真正的争论不是它们真不真，而是当人们发现它们是人造物之后，究竟该视其为随时可弃的枷锁，还是更需严肃共建的协作网络。
summaries.insight: 制度与共识从不悬浮在纯粹的语言或信念中，它高度依赖**物质载体与信息基础设施的硬度**。从刻在泥板上的汉谟拉比法典、跨大西洋的海底光缆，到银行核心系统的数据中心，任何社会实在要发挥效力，都必须消耗焦耳、占用服务器与金属线路。现代人之所以感知到信用分或国籍极其坚硬，并非仅因法律惩戒，更因它已被固化进自动化执行的算法流水线中。反之，一旦电网瘫痪或算力归零，最神圣的产权与最庞大的主权预期也会在几小时内坍缩。**社会建构的真实性，本质上是由承载它的物理与技术成本决定的**；看穿一套制度不能只解构其叙事，必须看清它锚定在怎样的物质技术堆栈之上。
summaries.advice:
1. **为精神内耗做一次「制度溯源」**：挑出一个本周最让你焦虑的规矩（如某项考核标准、世俗婚育年龄），花20分钟查明它的制定年份与历史背景；**看清它被发明的时间点与局限，打破其伪装成「自然规律」的心理强制**。
2. **将脆弱默契转为白纸黑字**：响应霍布斯的务实忠告，检查手头的一项关键合作或财产往来，在本周内补签一份书面备忘录或合同权责单，在彼此体面时引入第三方约束。
3. **自建不可妥协的微型秩序**：落实涂尔干对抗失范的方案，每周在固定时间安排一次线下面对面社交或物理运动，为浮动的生活主动铸造稳固的日常锚点。
summaries.summary_en: Regardless of whether they are labeled fictions, rituals, or emergent properties, these human constructs possess **undeniable causal efficacy**—they dictate the boundaries of physical action, allocate societal wealth, and decide who signs the consent form outside an ICU. No participant argues that these consequences can be wished away in private. The real fault line lies in what anchors this power: Hobbes grounds it in the monopoly of physical violence, Keynes and Harari in self-fulfilling shared expectations, while Durkheim and Rovelli locate it in macro-level, relational realities. The debate is less about whether these constructs are objectively real, and more about whether unmasking their human origins frees us to discard them or obligates us to steward them with greater care.
summaries.insight_en: Institutions and consensus do not float in the ether of pure language; they depend heavily on the **rigidity of material and informational infrastructure**. From Hammurabi's clay tablets to transoceanic fiber-optic cables and automated banking mainframes, any social reality requires joules, server racks, and physical copper to exert force. Modern citizens experience credit scores or borders as unyielding not just because of judges, but because they are hardcoded into automated, algorithmic pipelines. If the power grid fails, the most sacred property rights evaporate overnight. **The reality of any social construct is fundamentally anchored in the physical and computational costs required to sustain it**; understanding a system requires auditing its material stack, not just deconstructing its narrative.
summaries.advice_en:
1. **Conduct an institutional provenance check**: Pick one social expectation driving your current anxiety (e.g., a career milestone or a rigid KPI) and spend twenty minutes researching its origins. **Identify the exact historical moment it was invented to strip away its illusion of being an immutable law of nature.**
2. **Formalize fragile assumptions into writing**: Following Hobbes's pragmatic counsel, review a key personal or professional partnership this week and document expectations in a signed memorandum or clear contract while goodwill still prevails.
3. **Build your own micro-anchors**: Combat modern anomie, as Durkheim suggested, by scheduling a non-negotiable weekly in-person routine or physical training session to give your calendar a firm, tangible foundation.

hooks.text: **制度的电费**：一条产权、一个信用分、一本护照，要发挥效力都得消耗真实的焦耳——泥板、光缆、机房、常年通电的核心系统。我们习惯把社会实在讲成人与人之间的约定，却很少算它的物质账：一套共识能维持多久，也许取决于谁在替它付电费。若哪天算力与电网先松动，最坚硬的那几样会不会反而最早失效？
hooks.text_en: **The electricity bill of an institution**: a title deed, a credit score, a passport — each needs real joules to have any force: clay tablets once, now fibre, server halls and core systems that must never lose power. We are used to describing social reality as an agreement between people and rarely do its material accounting. How long a consensus can hold may come down to who is paying to keep it powered. If the grid and the compute give way first, will the hardest-seeming things be the earliest to fail?

hooks.text: **你的权利记在哪一本账上**：银行余额是账本上的一个状态，婚姻是登记与判决能调取的一种身份，学历是某个机构愿意背书的一行记录。于是同一件『真事』会在边界上突然失灵——在甲地成立的婚姻、产权、执照，到乙地可能查无此人。比起抽象地信错了故事，普通人更常见的风险是：不知道自己的权利记在哪里、谁认、拿什么证明、失败了向谁申诉。
hooks.text_en: **Which ledger is your right recorded in**: a bank balance is a state in a ledger, a marriage is a status that registries and courts can retrieve, a degree is a line some institution is willing to vouch for. Which is why the same 'real thing' can fail abruptly at a seam — a marriage, a title or a licence valid in one jurisdiction may return no record in another. The commoner risk for an ordinary person is not believing the wrong story in the abstract; it is not knowing where the right is recorded, who recognises it, what proves it, and where an appeal goes when recognition fails.

hooks.text: **换个称呼，到底改得动什么**：把裁员改叫优化，几天内就影响人怎么评价同一件事；一个新词进到语感里要几年；而母语里方位与性别那一层的偏置要一代人。同样是共同约定，硬度差着三个数量级。那么一场围绕称呼的争夺，究竟是在改现实，还是只在改第一层的权重。
hooks.text_en: **What does a change of name actually change**: rename layoffs as optimisation and within days it shifts how people rate the same event; for a new word to settle into the ear takes years; and the biases in a language's layer of space and gender take a generation. These are all conventions, and their hardness differs by three orders of magnitude. So when a fight breaks out over what something is called, is reality being changed, or only the weighting of the first layer?

hooks.text: **规矩松掉的那几年怎么过**：谈论制度是人造的，总是在它还立着的时候才从容。真正伤人的不是它太硬，是旧的失效而新的未立——婚姻、职业、社区同时松动的这些年，正是这种处境。一个人该怎样在没有现成刻度的时期，给自己造出几件够硬的东西？
hooks.text_en: **Getting through the years when the rules go slack**: it is always easy to discuss institutions as human constructions while they are still standing. What injures people is not that they are too hard but the stretch when the old ones have lapsed and the new ones are not yet laid down — which is precisely these years, with marriage, careers and neighbourhoods all loosening at once. How does a person build a few things hard enough to hold them during a period that supplies no ready-made scale?
